p: Preston is famous for the Preston Guild, a celebration held only once every twenty years. The last one was in 2012, and the next is due in 2032, so if you're around then, you're in for a treat. The saying 'once every Preston Guild' is still used across Lancashire to describe something that hardly ever happens.

Football has deep roots here too. Preston North End, who play at Deepdale, were one of the founding members of the Football League in 1888, and they won the first league title without losing a game, earning the nickname The Invincibles.
Preston Markets, with their grand Victorian canopy, are a great spot for food and local produce, and they're a short walk from the city centre.

For walkers and cyclists, the Guild Wheel is a 21-mile route that loops around the city, taking in countryside, riverside paths and parks. You don't have to do the whole thing, and there are plenty of shorter sections to enjoy.
Down by Preston Docks, the Ribble Steam Railway runs heritage trains and has a museum with locomotives, while the marina is a pleasant place to watch the boats.
With good motorway links and a central railway station, Preston is easy to reach from across Lancashire, and it's a great base for a family day out.

If the Ribble is calling, the riverside paths near Fishwick are an easy way into the Guild Wheel, and on a dry day a short stretch on foot or by bike is a lovely, gentle way to finish after the trampolines.
